title: A lower bound for the Ramsey number $r(3,3)$
statement:
Let $r(3,3)$ denote the Ramsey number for the pair $(3,3)$: the least natural number $n$ such that every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains either three mutually adjacent vertices (a triangle) or three mutually non-adjacent vertices (an independent set of size $3$). Then
\[
r(3,3) \ge 6.
\]
hypotheses_covered: none (bare lower-bound inequality on the Ramsey number r(3,3))
replaced:
\emph{\texttt{r(3, 3) $\ge$ 6}.}

\[r(3, 3) \geq 6 \qquad (7.8)\]

with the matching upper bound (\S{}7.2, p. 113):

Firstly, by (7.7) and (7.6)
\[r(3, 3) \leq r(3, 2) + r(2, 3) = 6\]
and therefore, using (7.8), we have $r(3, 3) = 6$.
